q: The production model should be selected using:
options: Validation results, with the test set used once at the end
explain: The test set stays out of all decisions.

options: Model versions and their stages, such as Production
explain: It says which version is live, and where it came from.

q: Why log ECE as well as AUC?
options: People read the probability, so its calibration matters
explain: A model can rank well and still give misleading probabilities.

q: Where do the fitted scaling statistics live at serving time?
explain: The pipeline goes with the model, which prevents skew.

options: Bagging reduces variance; boosting mainly reduces bias
Bagging reduces bias only; boosting has no effect
Both remove the need for data
explain: This is the central contrast of Module 3.

q: PSI above 0.2 on a key feature suggests you should:
options: Investigate, and consider retraining with a quality gate
explain: It's a signal to act on, and automatic replacement still needs a check.

q: Which matters for an honest end-to-end demo?
options: Every statistic was fitted on training data
The test set was used for tuning
Features differ between training and serving
explain: The other three are all kinds of leak or skew.

q: Stages in this program run from data to monitoring. How many stages does it print?
explain: 1 data, 2 experiments, 3 registered, 4 test, 5 packaged, 6 request, 7 monitoring.
